## Dev environment
### Set-up
To develop postcodElapse, Rstudio with the git large file storage (LFS) installed is required. [Instructions can be found here](https://git-lfs.com/). In addition, the following R packages are required: 

```r
install.packages(c("usethis", "pkgdown", "roxygen2")) #devtools

install.packages(c("dplyr", "terra","sf", "rlang")) #required by postcodElapse

install.packages(c("tidyverse", "tidyterra", "ggpubr")) #used in the docs
```

### Cloning
After installing all the dependencies, clone: https://github.com/GRIAC-Bioinformatics/postcodElapse. Make sure to enable git LFS for the repo and pull the large file, see shell commands below.

```bash
git lfs install

git lfs pull
```

This will download the 125MB ELAPSE.tif. Although it is too large for a normal commit, it is required by postcodElapse. If preferred, you can switch to the dev branch.

### Building
When implementing new features or fixing bugs, make sure to work on the dev branch. To quickly install the package in the Rstudio ribbon, navigate to: *Build > Load All*. This will quickly load the package into the current R session. Alternatively,  use the keybind: `Control + Shift + L`.

Again if you are implementing new features or fixing bugs please work on the `dev` branch. To quickly install the package in the Rstudio ribbon navigate: Build > Load All, this quickly loads the package into your R session. Or you can use the keybind: `Control + Shift + L`. 

To fully build the package in the ribbon: *Build > Install package* or use the `Control + Shift + B` keybind. , This will also update any changed documentation.

After finishing developing, to build postcodElapse for release on GitHub, use: *Run Build > Build Source Package*. This will build package as an archive (.tar.gz or .zip) in the parent directory of the repo. Add this file as new release to GitHub. Don’t forget to merge dev to main and update the documentation.

## Documentation

### In package
The package documentation is used for ?postcodElapse in R. It is created with roxygen from the comment blocks above the function definitions in the postcodElapse. See their [page](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/) for user information. 

### GitHub pages
More expanded guide style documentation can be found on the GitHub pages. This is created using *pkgdown*. Creating new articles or vignettes can be done with *usethis*, running in the R console `usethis::use_article()` or `usethis::use_vignette()`. User information can be found in the [pkgdown](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/) and [usethis](https://usethis.r-lib.org/) documentation.

Local building and viewing can be done by running `pkgdown::build_site()`. To publish the documentation on GitHub pages, run `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()` and wait until GitHub fully deploys the page.
